narrative:
The model estimated a 31.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk—roughly a three-in-ten chance of repayment difficulty. Although that is below an even chance, the bank’s approval standard is conservative, so this level was still too high and your application was denied.

The most influential factor was your savings position. Having at least 1,000 DM worked strongly in your favor, pushing toward good credit; only 2.9% of approved applicants had this level. The second most important factor was the loan’s purpose: a new-car request pushed toward bad credit, though it appears among 16.5% of approved cases. Third was your checking-account status: a 0–200 DM balance also pushed toward bad credit, a category seen among 18.4% of approved applicants. Together, these negative signals outweighed the positive savings signal.

To improve a future application, focus on strengthening your checking-account conduct and building a more stable savings record. You could also reconsider the borrowing purpose or amount, consider a guarantor, or ask the bank which criteria would make approval more likely.
